brief: Tech is range-bound at resistance, but GS, BofA and Nomura data frame the setup as skewed toward an upside breakout. Q2 S&P 500 EPS rose roughly 30% year-on-year even as AAII and GS sentiment stayed bearish. NDX shorts rose 35% since June and Q3 de-grossing pushed long/short net leverage to the 6th percentile, with gross tech exposure at the 43rd percentile and $163 billion cash on the sidelines, so GS calls the pain trade higher. GS's Flood, back from Asia where some hedge funds gave back more than 20% of YTD gains after July's momentum crash, found unusual caution and expects the coming IPO pipeline to draw investors back into risk. BofA says long-end yields hit multi-year highs on fiscal concerns but the tightening is far milder than 2022 (30-year drawdown roughly 7% versus more than 25%), and cites the dot-com boom, when the Nasdaq rallied over 200% as the 30-year yield rose about 200 basis points, as evidence tech can rally through rising rates. Nomura's McElligott flags a roughly $315 million AI options buyer reviving the spot-up, vol-up dynamic, and with bullish seasonality approaching, a breakout could turn into a chase.
